chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl from al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him): In
a man who died and left two maternal aunts and his clients (mawali), he said: 'Those of kinship are closer to one another in inheritance.' The wealth is divided between the two maternal aunts.

key_terms.مَوَالِيَهُ: His clients or freedmen, indicating manumission relationships

ai.seo_question: How is an estate divided when a man leaves only two maternal aunts and his mawali?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of 'Awl (proximity of kinship) is applied to determine that the two maternal aunts inherit the estate, overriding other potential claimants like the mawlā. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the Quranic verse 4:11 as a primary mechanism for distributing shares among collateral relatives when direct descendants or parents are absent. The case illustrates the practical application of kinship priority in the absence of closer male agnates.
